images.caption: Southern aspect of the main building of the (former) Royal Observatory, Cape of Good Hope, situated in Observatory, Cape Town. Construction commenced in 1825, with John Skirrow as contractor, and by 1829 regular astronomical observations were being carried out. The building initially had telescope domes on each of the south wings. These facilities were amalgamated with those of the South African   Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) in 1972, and the telescopes are currently housed at Sutherland in the Northern Cape.

images.caption: The Victoria telescope (also McClean telescope) consists of four telescopes on the same mount, including an 18-inch (for visible light) and 24-inch (for blue light) refractor, all built by Howard Grubb of Dublin. The Victoria dome and laboratory building were designed by sir Herbert Baker, and the dome was completed in 1896. The Victoria telescope was donated to the Royal Observatory by Frank McClean FRS (1837–1904) of Rusthall near Tunbridge Wells, England, for use by his colleague David Gill. It is currently a museum and visitor center and stands at the Royal Observatory, Cape of Good Hope, which since 1972 has been amalgamated with the South African Astronomical Observatory.[3][4]
